June 1919: Austria-Hungary was gone, and its successors were still fighting over where the lines would fall. One snapshot of the chaos.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ Czechs and Slovaks declared independence on 29 October 1918. The State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs was proclaimed the same day, then absorbed into the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes.

2/ Emperor Karl never formally abdicated. On 11 November 1918 he stepped back from state affairs in Austria, and two days later did the same for Hungary. German-Austria proclaimed a republic the next day.
3/ The dark red block in the middle is the Hungarian Soviet Republic, which lasted from 21 March to 1 August 1919. Béla Kun held the real power. The Entente blockaded it and never recognised it.
4/ It tried to expand. In June the Hungarian Red Army pushed into what is now Slovakia, and a short-lived Slovak Soviet Republic was proclaimed in Prešov on 16 June, the day after this map.
5/ Romania ended it. Romanian forces broke through Hungarian lines on 30 July. Kun fled to Vienna on 1 August, and Romanian troops entered Budapest days later.
6/ The final settlement came at Trianon on 4 June 1920. Hungary lost about 72% of its territory and 64% of its population, leaving roughly 3.3 million Hungarians as minorities abroad.
Which successor state on this map had the most improbable story? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
